content.section_11.2.1_Acute_decompensated_heart: Acutely decompensated heart failure (ADHF) is the most common form of AHF, accounting for approximately 50–70% of presentations. It usually occurs in patients with a history of heart failure and previous cardiac dysfunction across the spectrum of LVEF and may include right ventricular dysfunction. Distinct from the acute pulmonary oedema phenotype, ADHF typically has a more gradual onset; the main alteration is progressive fluid retention responsible for systemic congestion.
